findings.diagnosticMessage: 'GetByIdAsync' is called inside a loop body (repository call, lower confidence): potential query amplification
findings.mechanism: Per-order repository lookup executes once for every order, including repeated lookups when multiple orders share the same CustomerId, creating N I/O operations instead of one batched lookup.
findings.trigger: A request to /orders/summaries containing many orders, especially orders with duplicate or numerous customer IDs.
findings.fixDirection: Collect distinct customer IDs, fetch them with GetByIdsAsync before the loop, and resolve customers from the resulting dictionary.
findings.criticRationale: The /orders/summaries endpoint directly invokes the per-order GetByIdAsync path, with no batching or deduplication, so duplicate CustomerIds cause repeated repository calls.

verification.reason: verified by host benchmark template RepositoryCallAmplification/OrderCustomerLookup: value(n) ≥ 0.9·n for every n, and value(1000) ≥ 50·value(10)

findings.diagnosticMessage: 'GetByIdAsync' is called inside a loop body (repository call, lower confidence): potential query amplification
findings.mechanism: Product repository lookup runs inside the nested order-line loops, producing one sequential I/O operation per line and amplifying to the total number of lines across all orders; repeated ProductIds are fetched repeatedly.
findings.trigger: A request to /invoices containing many orders or orders with many lines, particularly when products recur across lines.
findings.fixDirection: Collect distinct product IDs, fetch products in a batch before iterating lines, and reuse the resulting lookup.
findings.criticRationale: The nested loop performs one repository call per line without deduplication, but the current repository is an in-memory Task.FromResult implementation rather than actual I/O.

findings.diagnosticMessage: Task.WhenAll starts one task per element of 'recipients', so concurrency grows with input size: potential unbounded fan-out
findings.mechanism: Task.WhenAll enumerates recipients and starts one SendAsync operation per element without a concurrency limit, so active notification work grows with the input size.
findings.trigger: A POST to /notifications containing a large recipients list causes all sends to be initiated at once, potentially exhausting downstream sender capacity, connections, or resources.
findings.fixDirection: Process recipients in sequential bounded batches or use a bounded concurrency gate such as SemaphoreSlim while preserving cancellation and exception propagation.
findings.criticRationale: The /notifications endpoint uses unbounded Task.WhenAll over all recipients, while the separate batched endpoint does not constrain this path.

verification.reason: verified by host benchmark template TaskFanOut/NotificationRecipients: value(n) ≥ 0.9·n for every n

findings.diagnosticMessage: Static collection field 'Reports' grows via Add and is never removed from or cleared in 'ReportCache': potential unbounded memory retention
findings.mechanism: The process-wide static Reports dictionary retains one Report object for every distinct key and has no eviction, size limit, removal, or clear operation.
findings.trigger: Requests to /reports/{key} using an unbounded stream of unique keys cause the dictionary and retained Report objects to grow for the lifetime of the process.
findings.fixDirection: Replace the static dictionary with a bounded cache using expiration and/or a size limit, or explicitly remove entries according to the required retention policy.
findings.criticRationale: The reachable /reports/{key} endpoint inserts every new key into a process-wide dictionary with no eviction, removal, clear, or size limit.

findings.mechanism: Each scoped OrderAuditHandler subscribes to the singleton OrderEventHub without unsubscribing, so the singleton event retains every handler instance and its delegate after the request scope ends.
findings.trigger: Repeated requests to /orders/placed create new scoped OrderAuditHandler instances; each subscription remains in OrderEventHub.OrderPlaced for the process lifetime.
findings.fixDirection: Implement IDisposable on OrderAuditHandler and unsubscribe from OrderEventHub.OrderPlaced during scope disposal, or change the lifetime/subscription design so the publisher does not outlive the handler.
findings.criticRationale: Each scoped handler subscribes to the singleton OrderEventHub and has no unsubscribe or disposal path, so the singleton event retains handlers across /orders/placed scopes.
